answer.concealment: confidentiality language modifications to the ISDA agreement with the banking counterparty
answer.actor: Sara Shackleton — the legal and regulatory coordinator who reviewed the counterparty's requested changes
answer.victim: Richard Sanders — the high-level legal reviewer and executive who must approve the agreement
answer.true_fact: The banking counterparty's requested confidentiality language removes the affiliate-disclosure carve-out, meaning Enron has no contractual permission to share deal terms with its affiliates under this ISDA agreement.
answer.false_belief: The standard affiliate-disclosure carve-out remains intact in the counterparty's proposed confidentiality language, preserving Enron's permission to disclose deal terms to affiliates for hedging purposes.

atoms.fact: The banking counterparty's proposed confidentiality language for the ISDA agreement — as set out in the changes forwarded on 2001-02-12 — contains no affiliate-disclosure carve-out; the four enumerated exceptions ((i) public availability, (ii) legal/regulatory compulsion, (iii) non-confidential source, (iv) the truncated fourth clause) do not include any provision permitting disclosure to affiliates for hedging or any other purpose.
Sara Shackleton knows that the banking counterparty's proposed confidentiality language contains no affiliate-disclosure carve-out.

Sara Shackleton tells Richard Sanders that the standard affiliate-disclosure carve-out is still present and operative in the counterparty's proposed confidentiality language, so Enron retains permission to share deal terms with affiliates for hedging purposes under the ISDA agreement.
